notes.title: New demo release for Invertigo
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

We have released an updated version of the demo of Invertigo today. Play it through Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1659520/Invertigo/

The new demo has a bunch of new functionalities and bugfixes. For example, you don't have to switch between the gravity modules anymore to use them. You can now use the gravity shift with the left mouse button and the gravity link with the right mouse button. 'E' can be used for the gravity hold module. Furthermore, the aforementioned controller support has been implemented. You can seamlessly switch between mouse and keyboard and controller while playing.

Other UI updates include an overhaul of the pause menu. The menu now contains both the scoreboard and the lore menu. The level select screen has also been reworked and is now also included on the main menu. The settings have been updated as well with for example a new 'invert mouse' option and an FOV slider.

And, as we showed in the last announcement, the game now starts with a level that combines the fan-favourite level Coffee Break with the mysterious room from the announcement. Because of this the old demo scoreboard for coffee break has to be wiped since that level no longer exists. Don't worry, the scoreboards for all the other levels will stay as they are :). To celebrate our original heroes who performed speedruns in the old coffee break, the top 100 hall of fame of that scoreboard will be posted in the high score channel of the discord to be immortalized. You can also see this top 100 here below.

So have fun playing the new demo! We're always happy to receive feedback to make Invertigo better, so let us know what you think.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/cc139a2dbeb7f94f4c815f74018fe22503df985e.png[/img]

Demo release changelog
- Removed gravity module switching, instead they can be invoked directly if available
- Added full gamepad support, with seamless switching
- Updated coffee break to have the official start of the game, along with new voice lines
- Added FOV slider
- Added invert mouse toggle
- Overhauled level selection menu
- Added save data (demo begins with all levels unlocked, but it will save anomaly/datalog collection)
- Added level select to main menu
- Added scoreboard and lore menu buttons to pause menu
- Gun screen now only gives visual feedback if the link module is enabled, and on picking up new modules
- Graphics presets actually work now

notes.title: Late Sunday Update!
notes.content:
Hello all! Surprise late Sunday update :)

[b]UI & UX[/b]
- Fix UI text bugs
- Make new mode pop-up properly disappear with custom binds and scroll wheel
- Fix fade after the last level not fading out if you switch level
- Fix sound volume level not initializing properly from settings
- Restart no longer brings you to the previous level if done in starting airlock

[b]Scoreboard[/b]
- Fix bug with moves scores not saving properly
- Make "around you" scroll to your entry properly on the scoreboard
- Fix histogram not properly marking the bar you're in

[b]Movement & Mechanics[/b]
- Smooth velocity over force zones in all directions:
    - Fix horizontal velocity not resetting after landing from jump
    - Reset horizontal velocity after some air-time
- Increased air control and decrease jump momentum preservation to compensate
- Fix view slowly centering

[b]Levels & Visuals[/b]
- Fixed glitch spots where your head sticks out of bounds and you can see the whole outside 
- Added some easter eggs
- Added a thank-you for Creem and the speedrunning folks at Discord, you're awesome!
- Cleaned up geometry (overlapping meshes, Z-fighting)
- Cleaned up lighting (colors, values, placement)
- Patched up various holes on all levels
- Changed lever visuals to be more clear
- Cleaned up collision for several objects

- Reposition one of the moving pillars on Greenhouse
- Fixed the 'trap yourself in the red room' in the Coffee Break
- Deleted unnecessary meshes from levels
- Reduced size of lightmaps

Thanks a lot to all the folks who joined our Discord recently and made bug reports, we tried to squash as many of the bugs as we could. We will soon post a status update about some exciting new maps that we are working on!

Now get back to speedrunning!

notes.title: Invertigo Update: improved gravity shifts and scoreboard
notes.content:
While we are still working hard on the full version of the game, we thought we could already provide you with some fixes and new features with an update of the demo. You can update the free demo of Invertigo on Steam as of today. This update contains the following fixes and features.

Improved gravity shifts
*The view tries to level with the floor now
*A speed curve is used to reduce motion sickness
*Gravity shifts in general are faster and smoother

Improved scoreboard
*Developer scores can be toggled on, which means you can also compete with our times if you want
*The histogram to look at the distribution of results from the community has been improved
*Steam avatars and as well as Steam friend icons are now included
*The scoreboard is now also scrollable

And one more thing: the gravity tool can now only be used after you open the door of the airlock. The era of speedrunning while doing all your moves inside the airlock is over.

*The histogram to look at the distribution of results from the community has been improved
*Steam avatars and as well as Steam friend icons are now included
*The scoreboard is now also scrollable

notes.title: Progress update
notes.content:
Since our last announcement we've continued to work on the detailed design of multiple of our total of 25 levels. Two levels which we'd like to share with you are called 'coffee break' and 'equipment bay'. Coffee break is one of the earliest levels in the game as is intended as a place for staff on the station to relax. It is connected to a lot of other elements of the ship and as such it has a maze-like aesthetic to it. Here below are a few screenshots of the level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/84a4276aac67484fb6d4f70532879638ed6878cf.jpg[/img]

The second level comes along quite a bit later into the game and is called the equipment bay. As the name suggests it is used to store parts of the station and contains tools to fix any damage to the facility.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/d0c7e59961a6178346993d5989d3e95d72b909cd.png[/img]

Finally, we'd like to mention a few technical fixes and developments. The movement-related mechanics have received a full overhaul to make it feel more natural and to fix issues such as the ability to slide over steep slopes. Similarly, the gravity tool mechanics have been updated. One example is the gravity plane change move, which used to position the player slightly to the side of where they wanted to go. However, with these fixes this problem has been resolved.

One example is the gravity plane change move, which used to position the player slightly to the side of where they wanted to go. However, with these fixes this problem has been resolved.

notes.title: Progress update
notes.content:
Since our last announcement we've been working on new assets and functionalities which we've directly implemented into the greenhouse level, a level which you might've already seen a few times in previous announcements. We'll go over the updates one by one. Firstly, we now have six new differently sized wall panels which allow for a much more varied aesthetic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/27749721aa6f9885a713277662dd25162662ed4b.png[/img]

The greenhouse level in general has been updated significantly with new assets and updated lighting. The plants still need to be added, but the level is very close to being done.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/3e565126160eefecd044e0a07c6731779fc0c521.png[/img]

When you play the eventual version of the game, be on the lookout for any easter eggs or hidden rooms. We already mentioned the data logs which can be found in each level, but there's also for example this secret room.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/de9f241d75c00ec736e03441bf7a5ae893d27858.png[/img]

Finally, a lot of new pillar models have been made which can be used as support structures or platforms from which to jump to other parts of the level. The big vent level from a few announcements ago will for example make use of these.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/959c555d9356b9b55450dcc1011d3a3bdf069123.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Progress update
notes.content:
It's been a while since the last announcement and we've made a lot of progress since then that we'd like to share with you. Firstly, we've been working on some new levels. One of these is currently known as the 'pantry level'. A blockout with basic lighting has been made, which you can see below. The level starts in a reddish industrial area and eventually ends with a puzzle based on the concept art from the previous announcement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/221fe381902a0342560cb5a5b6466f26f19fde55.png[/img]

Secondly, the pillars shown in the previous announcement have now been implemented and can extend based on triggers in the level such as pressure plates or timers. The pillars themselves have also received slight upgrades to their design and panels have been made to surround and encase the pillars.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/c8e9b3dee3002b58b096f8c15261513f184c9b35.gif[/img]

Finally, the game now also supports triggerable force fields. These can for example be used to activate a stream of particles with a lever as can be seen below. These particles can also induce a force to push the player into a specific direction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/2ac789fdd966dbc49635696e7b492a7d97e144a6.gif[/img]

notes.title: Progress update
notes.content:
We've continued working on Invertigo the last few weeks and here's some of our progress. Firstly, we've made a few more assets for the game. This includes foliage models for the greenhouse level. You can see some of the new plants models below. We've also expanded tweaked the pillar models and added versions with broken glass.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/debcc29eaf797f95d90959b7a00f2ca5c1742cc7.png[/img]

Secondly, we also have some new concept art to share. Specifically, we've been working on concept art for the pantry/kitchen level. The eventual version of the level will contain conveyor belts and many different food items, but even without that the current concept art should already give you a good idea of the kind of gravity bending puzzles we want to implement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/75aca89e4bfa78cdc3d6b24ae5fe8b7cf3cdba68.png[/img]

Thirdly, we'd like to mention a few other additions and bug fixes. The system to implement data logs into the game, shown with the concept art a few announcements ago, has now been implemented into the game. The data logs can be accessed by interacting with control panels throughout the levels. Furthermore, we've fixed the bug that caused batteries and other objects to glitch through the walls of the level and disappear. A bug that prevented players from jumping when standing on the edge of a platform has also been resolved.

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
On behalf of the Invertigo development team, a happy new year to all of you. In the last few weeks we've enjoyed our nice winter holiday (we hope you did too) and now we're back and ready to continue working on Invertigo. Here I'd like to share some of our progress of the past weeks. Firstly, we've continued working on new concept art. This ranges from a rough schematic overview of the puzzle (left image) to fullly fledged artwork (right image).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/9d7bc7013621725da1ec9f78310e44ffd70e7517.png[/img]

Some artwork assets have now also been implemented in the game. One example of this is a new door model. The image below shows the old door model to the right and the new model on the left.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/c6853dbd3285ae0b4554ffd5fd49eb2e7e17dcbd.png[/img]

Finally, we wanted to show you the progress we've made on the remake of level 3 since our last announcement. We have a lot of exciting things that we're working on and can't wait to show them to you so stay tuned for our next announcement later this month.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/720b85f3a7454724933f92df3c944057759ea9d9.png[/img]

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
We wanted to keep you up to date on our latest progress, so here's another announcement with exciting developments that we want to share with you. Firstly, we'd like to show you detailed blender models and sketches of some of the items that you might have already seen in the previous screenshots of level 1. Below you can see a new bench model, as well as concept art as a blender model for the life support pod from which the player wakes up.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/4919aa2c8e59fe8010d1fe059df36f8e2f723faf.png[/img]

We've also been working on other artwork related assets. The gravity stations, where the player can get the different modes of the gravity tool, have been redesigned and now look more like glowing disks on the floor as you can see here. You can also see some possible redesigns for other items such as elevator panels and the batteries (red blocks).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/4a9e3abd055cdad8e9183635b71708fd980430ff.png[/img]

Finally, we've been working on a lot of extra levels. Some of the feedback we received is that there is a steep learning curve regarding the gravity tool modes at the start of the game and therefore we're busy adding multiple easier tutorial-like levels so the player can get acquainted with the new mechanics. Here you can see a few screenshots of those levels in different stages of completion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/c6e69625914eb8002a87970d9958b0dff8f18a7a.png[/img]

tags.feature: Finally, we've been working on a lot of extra levels.

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
It's been a while since our last update, but since then we've made a lot of exciting progress that we can't wait to share with you. Firstly, we worked on the very first level of the game, a level that does not yet exist in the demo. This is the room in which the player wakes up from a cocoon-like life support tank. Here's a snapshot of the current version of the level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/08dcbe3f2fe21f971700494970d4c6338ef253be.png[/img]

We're still continuing to work on this level and have some cool concept art to share with you about our idea of the eventual version of the level. Check out this artwork for the room where the player wakes up.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/d142b6e167f21d486f78f3912174c1d2113c8edf.jpg[/img]

As well as this concept art for the so-called 'decontamination tunnel'. The current state of the tunnel can be seen in the left image.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/2a585e27fe2c0c7cfb7bd092a0286a8782c14b11.png[/img]

Finally, there are some bug fixes that we want to mention. There has been an upgrade to pressure plates which now prevents the plate element from going through walls or from getting stuck. Furthermore, in the current demo the grab tool sometimes rotates and accelerates blocks in an unexpected manner, causing them to 'jump' when released. This especially happened if you moved the block rapidly. As you can see in the gif below, this has now been fixed. So no more flying battery blocks!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/cef1c130916608d9735d1b4574e9f940ed7c3855.gif[/img]
